Notes to Authors

It the policy of this Journal to publish articles in English in all fields of ISLAM provided they are of a high caliber and contribute to the fundamental knowledge of the religion. In keeping with the universal nature of Islam, this journal is not intended to reflect any political, regional, or nationalistic bias. Articles containing unwarranted attacks, direct or implied, against any other religion, sect, belief, or ideology, shall not be accepted for publication. The journal's sole objective is to work within the framework of ISLAM towards a full appreciation of God's message to all humanity.

The journal recognizes the sources of Islamic knowledge to be the Qur'an, the Sunna, analogy (Qiyas), consensus (Ijma'), and personal thought (Ijtihad). However, THE QUR'AN shall be the ultimate reference. Only statements in full agreement with the Qur'an shall represent the journal's official stand. All other statements, or statements subject to various interpretations shall represent only the author's personal viewpoint.

Manuscripts submitted for publication should be typed, double spaced. Only one copy is required. All Qur'anic quotations must be accompanied by the number(s) of sura(s), and the number(s) of verse(s). Colons should separate the number of sura from the number(s) of verse(s) (e.g. 17:28-33). A group of verses from the same sura should be separated from each other by commas (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62). When more than one sura are involved, a semi-colon should separate the different suras (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62; 23:16; 36:9-11, 19-25, 44). The journal will undertake to add the Arabic text to all Qur'anic translations. This is to avoid the inadvertent mental re-translation to an Arabic composition which is different from the original.

Every Hadith should be accompanied by its sources (transmitters) and the reference book where it may be found. If the transmitter(s) and/or the reference book were not known, this should be stated clearly.

Transliteration of Arabic words and names should follow the convention shown below. The only vowels should be: i (as in ibn), a (as in Ahmad), u (as in ummah), i-long (as in tafsir), a-long (as in ayat), and u-long (as in Hud).

ISLAM: Its Mission in the World
2. CONDEMNATION OF THE PRINCIPLE OF BLIND IMITATION
by Professor M. Farid Wajdi

Of all his achievements as writer, editor of Nour-el-Islam, and Professor at Al-Azhar University, Dr. Wajdi is better known for his famous Qur'anic commentary. This series of articles, which were written by him in Arabic, promises to be a most cherished feature by ALL readers of Islam.

In all ages throughout the human history, reformers were never confronted with a stronger obstacle than that of blind imitation of forefathers and leaders of old religions. This inaction has been the cause of the persistence to this day of corrupted religions whose survival in our times is a slur on the human intellect. It was equally responsible for the continual existence of certain sects which exploited the ignorance of people who were otherwise well-fitted to take their place among the rising nations but have for this reason remained in stygian darkness down to the present day.

Only one who has made a thorough study of the religions professed by the majority of contemporary nations as well as of the few hundred minor divisions derived therefrom, could appreciate the pernicious influence exercised by blind imitation over the life of people and the harm involved in the consequent antagonism to learning and reason. Next to the establishment of its principal beliefs, Islam has striven against the tendency of blind imitation into which people have long lapsed without having it examined or assayed by reason.

Indeed, this rational idea could never have been conceived by minds in those dark and remote times when humanity was yet under age. But when humanity attained maturity in the generations that followed, this idea became an essential element of the universal religion which was ordained by the Lord in His last dispensation, not only to conform with the momentous intellectual development that took place, but also to rouse the religious sentiment in the hearts of men and inspire them to still greater and higher attainments.

Those interested in the investigation of human affairs of recent times will find out that souls have discarded all moral restraints and have fallen an easy prey to unbridled passion and wickedness while the religious sentiment

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 85-90

ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

which constitutes the supreme moral power mitigating those excesses, has become incapable to discharge its function in many a nation. It was on account of this that other agents were sought to counteract those excesses. Some have sought such agents in science, in the power of public opinion or in some human instinct. But the investigator who goes deeply into the initial causes of things, will soon realize that, of all human instincts, the religious sentiment is best suited to counteract those excesses and to wield the most beneficial influence over the souls of men. If, however, it has become unequal to the task in certain nations, it is only on account of the weakness which affected their religions and which was the outcome of what was impressed on the people as being traditional matters to be followed or disregarded as a whole. But if they knew that a religion existed which severely censures imitation and imitators, and insists on reasoning and consideration, a religion whose beliefs are founded on evidence and truth, and is withal framed in a system which surpasses that of modern scientific investigation in reasoning and accuracy, their hopes in regaining the influence of religion will be roused again. For once this influence is regained the religious sentiment is awakened and its power will once more be felt in the guidance of men and in setting up a virtuous civilization for the world.

It was for this reason that Islam has striven hard to overcome the obstacle of blind imitation and has attempted to do this by different ways of reasoning aiming thereby at three objects:
1. To spread its life-giving principles calculated to revive humanity in its later days.
2. To conserve for the religious sentiment its intrinsic power which enables it to restrain the human passions and safeguard the people from being carried away by wickedness.
3. To render the system of religious investigation more advanced and more accurate than that of scientific investigation so that the latter may not overwhelm the former and put it into insignificance.

This is a great objective at which Islam aimed so that reason may not hold undisputed sway over souls independent of the religious sentiment which the Lord has set to mitigate the brutal tendencies attendant on the human state and which no intellectual culture could restrain.

This could only come about by convincing reason, by proof, to give due regard to that sentiment and to admit the power exercised by it. Thus, reason will not concede unless that sentiment is established on a like system of research and investigation and is equally free of any traces of imitation unsupported by material or mental evidence.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

M. Farid Wajdi

By so doing, Islam has succeeded to associate reason with the religious sentiment for the first time in the history of religions. It has succeeded, on the strength of these two great principles, to raise a nation which attained to the height of human progress and took the lead in both moral and scientific culture as well as in the religious leadership of the world. Islam was thus rendered equal to establish the highest civilization on earth without the conflict between religion and reason and without people degenerating in their morals and propensities as is the case in the present day civilization.

Let us now consider how far has Islam succeeded to fulfill this great project.

Islam was revealed at a time when people were the slaves of false and corrupted religions which they inherited from their forefathers and from which they could not be moved. Any one who wished to move them therefrom was regarded by them as a bitter enemy merely because he attempted to bring about a reform.

The campaign was first opened by admonitions and threats thus awakening in men the instinct of reasoning and urging them to reflection and consideration of the sad end to which past nations have come. This done, Islam began to attack the main cause which prevented them to consider any reform viz. the blind imitation of their forefathers even though they were completely in the wrong. In this connection the Lord says:

And when they are told, "You shall follow what God has sent down," they say, "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers lacked both knowledge and guidance?
The allegory of those who disbelieve is like those who parrot whatever they hear without any understanding. They are deaf, dumb, and blind. Thus, they fail to understand. (2:170-171)

In the preceding verses, the Lord has given a representation of the state of those who were blinded by imitation. He who calls them to righteousness is likened to one who parrots whatever he hears without any comprehension. They are deaf, dumb, blind and devoid of understanding on account of their holding fast to the practices of their forefathers and refusing to put them to the test of reason.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

The Lord says that if those unbelievers were asked to follow what the Lord has sent down, they will say "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing," to which the Lord replies rousing the instinct of reason in them: "What if their forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?"

Then the Lord gave the above representation of them which no one with a whit of pride would tolerate, provoking them thereby to seek an outlet to their sorry state.

In order to move them from this inaction, the Lord then applies different reasoning.

And when they are told, "Come to what God has sent down; come to this Messenger," they say, "Enough for us is what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers had neither knowledge, nor guidance? (5:104)

That is, if the unbelievers were called to follow the guidance of the Qur'an they say the knowledge which we inherited from our forefathers is sufficient for us to which the Lord says:

"Will you still say so if your forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?"

And in this connection the Lord demanded of the unbelievers to support their claim of the so-called knowledge of their forefathers:

Have you any certain knowledge to substantiate your claim that you may produce to us? (6:148)

In another verse the Lord says [printed as "days" in the original, apparent typo]:

Bring me a scripture before the Qur'an or some vestiges of ancient knowledge to support your claim if you are truthful. (46:4)

In describing the end of those who imitate their forefathers without any knowledge or a book to guide them, the Lord says:

That is when the leaders shall disown their followers. They shall undergo the punishment and no help shall come to them. The followers shall then say, "If we only get a second chance, we shall disown them as they have disowned us." Thus, God will show them the consequences of their deeds; nothing but sorrow for them, and they shall never exit from the hellfire. (2:166,167)

And:

The Lord will say unto the unbelievers on the Judgment day: "Enter ye into Hell together with nations of jinn and of men who have preceded you;" so oft as one nation enters, it shall curse its sister, until they have all entered in succession, the last of them shall say unto the first: "O Lord, these have led us astray, deal Thou unto them a double punishment of hell-fire;" and the Lord will say: "It shall be doubled unto all, but ye know not."
And the first of them shall say unto the last: "Ye have no advantage over us and we have both been in error; taste ye therefore the punishment for that which ye have done." (7:38-39)

In the preceding verses, the Lord points out that the followers of disbelief are just as culpable as the leaders, for the Lord has endowed all men with reason and required them to distinguish between truth and falsehood. They are therefore equally responsible for their deeds and none of them has an advantage over the other. And when the imitators have asked the Lord to deal a double punishment to their leaders whose example they have imitated, the Lord has adjudged them both responsible and has doubled the punishment to them all. Such was the Lord's warning against persistence in blind imitation.

In another chapter of the Qur'an the Lord says:

Unto the leaders it shall be said:
"This is a company which shall be plunged with you into Hell," to which they shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they shall burn in hell-fire like us." And the followers shall say unto the leaders: "But ye, too! There shall be no welcome for you. It was ye who brought us to this and wretched is the abode." (38:59-60)

On the entry of the unbelievers into Hell, angels shall say to the leaders: "This is a company of your followers that shall be plunged with you into Hell." The leaders shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they have had minds to distinguish between truth and falsehood and their punishment is hell-fire like us." The followers will retort: "No welcome for you either, you have enticed us into this delusion and wretched indeed is our ending."

The Lord (may He be praised and glorified!) has seen fit to impress on us by such variegated forms of eloquence the fact that leaders and followers will come to the one and same evil end, and it avails the latter not to be followers of others so long as they have had minds by which to distinguish between truth and falsehood.

By these solemn admonitions, Islam has demolished the principle of blind imitation of forefathers and has awakened the conciousness of individual responsibility. It has delivered the weak from their bondage to the strong and smashed down the invulnerable walls of exclusiveness which the leaders raised for their own ends.

By demolishing blind imitation Islam has aimed at abolishing a state of ignorance in which men were enslaved to certain sects that made learning and religion an exclusive right only to themselves, and arbitrarily ruled the people even as absolute masters do. They suffered no censure or criticism to be passed on their actions and declined the admission, into their exclusive body, of any outsider though he may have been a noted man of learning and genius.

Should this state of things become established in a nation, learning and religion will be rendered the exclusive right of a sect which will exploit them in their own interest and subject them to the dictates of their passion. In course of time, they will become a collection of stereotyped forms which will check the onward march of progress and stand between nations and the realization of their objectives.

Freedom from the shackles of imitation was the objective of Islam and it has led its people to a perfect state of cooperation between learning and religion as well as between sentiment and reason. Through this cooperation Muslims have attained to the height of progress which gave them the world-leadership for many a century and it is assured that they will regain that leadership once they follow faithfully, the tenets of their glorious religion.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY: THE ULTIMATE PROOF OF AUTHENTICITY*
by Yusuf Amin Wali, Ph.D.
Treasurer, Supreme Council of the Muslim Young Men's Association, Cairo, Egypt

God's finalized and completed message delivered in the Arabic language.** However, since it is intended for all the people, in all places, at all the times, it carries within its composition the proof of authenticity which can be understood and fully appreciated by anyone regardless of his tongue. On these pages, the reader is presented with physical, examinable, and indisputable evidence that the Qur'an is the unaltered message from the Almighty to His creation. Seekers of the truth shall find herein sure guidance towards their goal. The unfortunate souls who are afflicted with various prejudices shall be utterly blinded (Qur'an 18:57)

The greatest affliction of man is the lack of identity and purpose. Once a correct identity is established, and once the purpose behind our existence is defined, such affliction can, sequentially, be removed. The vast majority of people spend their lives under the pretense that the body constitutes one's identity. Thus, they spend their lives caring for the body, the mere shell of their real self; working, laboring, fighting among themselves, hating, loving, and struggling in the service of their vanishing entity. When it is too late, i.e., when they shed the shell, they discover that their real self was left unfed, undeveloped, and miserably neglected. Their eternal existence in such a feeble state can be rightly described as "hell." On the other hand, those who are fortunate enough to overcome this identity crisis will be able to define their purpose, place the emphasis during their earthly existence on the right goal, and live and act accordingly. They will realize that developing their eternal entity requires putting the body in the service of the soul, and not the other way around.

*Condensed from the book "Miracle of the Qur'an: Significance of the Mysterious Alphabets" by Rashad Khalifa, Islamic Productions International, Inc., St. Louis, Missouri, USA. 1973.
**It had to be delivered in some language. The Qur'an itself states that its language is immaterial; that the believers shall grasp the full message therein, regardless of their mother tongue; and that even the Arabic-speaking people will not understand it unless they qualify therefor by sincerity and devotion (6:25, 18:57; 4:44; 56:77-79.)

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 91-104

GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

Our Creator has informed us of the ways and means of developing and caring for the soul. His message, the one and only message, started with the creation of Adam, the first man; the first messenger. Subsequent messengers, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad (may God bestow His blessings and peace upon them), delivered the same message whereby man can feed and develop his real self. With the arrival of God's final messenger, THE MESSAGE was finalized, and the Almighty Himself vowed to preserve it for all subsequent generations, and to protect it from alteration or distortion(1). Moreover, the Almighty has vowed to embed in His message such proof of authenticity that each generation can witness; leaving no excuse for anyone to disbelieve(2). This article, which is but a glimpse from a vast computerized study of the Qur'an (3), offers an example of the visible miracles which are embedded in the Qur'an to prove its authenticity. Only those completely enslaved by worldly matters will deny the indisputable proof presented here. To appreciate this evidence which comes to all of humanity from their Creator, one needs no special knowledge of the Qur'an's language.

The Qur'anic Initials

One of the unique features of the Qur'an is the occurrence at the beginning of certain suras of alphabets which bear no apparent meanings. These alphabets, henceforth called "Qur'anic Initials," are not known in any other literary work.

Of the 114 suras in the Qur'an 28 begin with one set of Qur'anic initials, and one sura is prefixed with two sets of Qur'anic initials. Each set of Qur'anic initials consists of a number of letters ranging between one and five. The different sets of Qur'anic initials and the suras where they occur are listed in Table 1. As shown in that table, there are 14 different sets of Qur'anic initials, and the number of letters which participate in the make-up of these initials is also 14. The 14 letters involved in the formation of Qur'anic initials are Alif (A), Ha (H), Ra (R), Sin (S), Sad (S), Ta (T), 'Ayn ('A), Qaf (Q), Kaf (K), Lam (L), Mim (M), Nun (N), Ha (H), and Ya (Y). These letters are known in the Muslim literature, more specifically among the Sufi mystics, as "the illumination letters." The other half of the alphabet, the 14 letters not involved, are known as "the darkness letters."

The suras which contain Qur'anic initials are listed in their recorded sequence in Table 2.

Race, Racism and Islam

The phenomenal scientific and sociological development of the 20th century Western world has had little effect on the growing problem of race relations. Man reaches for the moon and stars, but finds it difficult to extend the hand of brotherhood to fellow travellers on space ship Earth. Islam provided solutions to the racial problem 1400 years ago, in theory and in practice, without the need for demonstrations or civil rights bills. It established a society based on racial respect and mutual appreciation. Islamic principles thus contain the unfaltering light necessary to lead mankind out of the darkness and ignorance of racial discord.

Racial Concepts

Racism has reference to a socio-political policy or system which is based on the exaggeration of racial differences or on prejudice in favor of a certain race. Race itself is difficult to define. Many writers have spoken customarily of a Greek "race", a Nordic "race", an Anglo-Saxon "race", an Aryan "race" and so on, but racial nomenclature is illusive. Though mankind is comprised of a number of different groups which are physically distinguishable in some degree from one another, "the differences between the four major groups of man and between the ethnic groups comprising them merely represent a distribution of variations which... occur more frequently in one group than they do in another... Not one of the major groups of man is unmixed, nor is any one of its ethnic groups pure; all are, indeed, much mixed and of exceedingly complex descent. Nor is there any scientific justification for overzealous or emotional claims that any one of them is in any way superior to another."(1) In general, "race" means the major divisions of mankind which share certain common physical characteristics such as skin color, facial structure and texture of hair. But such has been the distribution and free mingling of mankind over the millenia that these classifications are more arbitrary than absolute. There are no pure races. Those who decry or bemoan "race mixing" are several thousand years too late.

Although there is no scientific justification for a dogma of either racial superiority or racial inferiority, the past century has witnessed increasing efforts to invest racism with a scientific sanction. "In the universities... Southern whites received substantial though indirect support by racist scholars

Islam and Africans

Some noted authors have asserted incorrectly that Muslim travelers did not think highly of Africans, with special reference to the manner in which some

of them characterized the Zanj.(6) But the term Zanj in Muslim writing does not refer to all Africans. What they found offensive was certain aspects of the pagan culture of the Zanj, not their race, and the Muslim writers never connected blackness of skin with inherent inferiority. Instead, they sought to explain the variations of skin color in terms of geography. They wrote that the racial characteristics of Europeans resulted from a cool, northern clime, while the racial traits of Africans derived from the hot, southern clime. Their observations convinced them that neither whites nor blacks had a monopoly on either intelligence or ignorance. The actual enshrining of discrimination on the pedestal of science, however, awaited later centuries.

Race in the Early Muslim Community

No proper assessment of the Islamic attitude on race can be made without primary reference to the examples of the prophet Muhammad (peace be

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

S. Shahid Mufassir

upon him) and his companions (may God be pleased with them). These examples, together with the guidance of God in the Qur'an are what constitute the Islamic position on race. It is not sufficient to scrutinize the concepts of a certain traveler, merchant, wali or sultan 300 or 700 years after the Hijrah to formulate an indication of Islam's racial standards. Confusing the personal attitudes of individual Muslims with that of the Islamic law or community inevitably leads to incomplete and incorrect conclusions.

We are met first of all with the striking observation that of all the great prophets ONLY Muhammad had an intimate companion of the African race. Therefore, the prophet (peace be upon him) provided an excellent, instructive example of Islamic racial attitudes in his companionship with Bilal b. Rabah, the Ethiopian whom Abu Bakr ransomed from slavery to pagan Arabs. Consequent to the Hijrah to Madinah, the prophet joined the Muhajirun with ansari families in a socio-economic brotherhood which abolished all distinction between Makkan and Madinan Muslims, between Quraysh and Aus or Khazraj tribes, between freeman and former slave. Bilal was joined in brotherhood with Abu Ruwayha of the Arab family of Khas'am. There was no social segregation; there were no frantic efforts to find another black family with which to join Bilal. In 20th century industrialized societies minorities are often assigned to menial positions reserved for social outcasts or inferiors. The Muslims did not treat Bilal in this manner. Indeed, he was appointed the treasurer of the Muslim community, a position of utmost responsibility and trust. Bilal was renowned also as the first mu'adhdhin, which was a position of respected spiritual leadership. He was an active participant — not an orderly or attendant — in all of the battles fought to defend the Muslim community, slaying in the battle of Badr his former owner, Umayyah. There is no analogy at all to the degrading references to blacks even in America in the case of Bilal. The Muslims never called him a "nigger", a "coon" or a "Sambo". Rather, this former slave was affectionately called "Sayyiduna Bilal" — our master Bilal — by the Muslims.

Similarly, in America and most European countries, racial intermarriage has long been legally taboo, just as it still is in white-ruled nations like Rhodesia and South Africa. Despite the claims to being representative of the greatest civilzation, sophistication and Christian brotherhood, many American whites continue to denounce intermarriage between blacks and whites as undesirable. When they refer to it as miscegenation they infer that the mis- is the prefix for bad or wrong (though the real derivation is from Latin miscere, to mix). For them, all race mixing is bad and wrong, even though mankind has been doing just that since time immemorial. Here also the example of Bilal is instructive. The Muslims set up no barriers of law or custom to "protect" the noble Arab ladies from marriage to non-Arabs

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

RACE, RACISM AND ISLAM

generally or Africans in particular. Bilal married not one, but several Arab ladies of respected lineage before his death in Damascus at 63 years of age.(11) There can be no reasonable doubt as to the sincerity of the Muslims in treating all people with dignity and equality.

Those writers who assert that traditions in which Bilal is given permission to marry an Arab girl are "probably not authentic" call their own scholarship into serious question, especially since they accept without question obviously spurious traditions such as the one in which the prophet is supposed to have said, "Do not bring black into your pedigree," or another ridiculous tradition which warned, "Do not intermarry with the sons of Ham." Even before Islam, black Arabs like 'Antar were considered heroes and the doctrine that the sons of Ham, allegedly the black race, were cursed is not a Muslim legend, as erroneously stated by some writers.(12) This theory is based on a misunderstanding of words recorded in the Bible at Genesis 9:25, 26 where the curse is actually put upon Canaan, not Ham. However, the Jewish Babylonian Talmud of the 6th century CE transmitted the misconception that "the descendants of Ham are cursed by being black". Benjamin of Tudela, a Spanish rabbi of the 12th century CE inscribed that "there is a people... who, like animals... go about naked and have not the intelligence of ordinary men... these sons of Ham are black slaves."(13) Likewise, Christian writers picked up this mistaken theme from the Bible. In 1577, George Best explained the black skin of the African as ultimately the result of the curse on Ham, whose son Cush and "all his posterity after him should be so black and loathesome that it might remain a spectacle of disobedience to all the world. And of this black and cursed Cush came all these black Moors which are in Africa."(14) Interestingly, in his religious bias, Best included the "Moors" (African Muslims) in the curse.

There are clear, authentic traditions in which the Prophet declares unreservedly that there is no superiority for an Arab over a non-Arab so far as race is concerned.(15) Furthermore, no intelligent Arab would specifically condemn intermarriage with the "sons of Ham" because the "sons of Ham" include the Egyptians of old. (Egypt is called the "land of Ham" in the Bible at Psalms 78:51 and elsewhere.) Hajira (Hagar), the mother of the Arabs, was Egyptian and so was Mariya, the wife of Muhammad. Egypt, of course, is geographically African and racially heterogeneous, and has been racially mixed since the days of the early pharoahs.(16) In 1933, discoveries of prehistoric paintings in North Africa (near present-day Djanet in Algerian sahara) cast interesting light on the racial heterogeneity of that entire area. "At Tin Aboteka there is the figure of a huge archer, almost two meters tall, with Negroid features... From a careful study of details and features, it is evident that the first authors of the paintings were a Negroid

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

S. Shahid Mufassir

hunting people. This is a very interesting fact because it proves that the range of the Negroid element in Africa in prehistoric times reached much farther northward* than it does today... the paintings, characterized by human figures with round heads, date back to circa 6000-7000 B.C.... Another noticeable element in these paintings is the variety of racial types coexisting as of a certain period. Side by side with the original Negroid element are figures with clearly Mediterranean profiles, or Ethiopians, a fact which confirms what was already known about the ethnic composition of the ancient Saharan peoples but which sheds new light on the relations between them. At a certain point these groups lived side by side in this region." (Dr. Giorgio Gualco, "The Rock Paintings of Tassili," in Mankind magazine, vol. 4, no. 6, April, 1974, pp. 41-47. emphasis added.) Much the same can be said of the ancient Egyptian paintings. Pharoahs and commoners alike were often portrayed with "Negroid" features. (See Egyptian Art, ed. by Francesco Abbate, Octopus Books: London, 1972.)

As reported by a ninth century C.E. Muslim writer of African descent, Muslim society imposed no barriers to intermarriage. According to Al-Jahiz of Basra, "the deserts swarm with the number of our (African) men who married your (Arab) women and who became chiefs and defended you against your enemies." (Kitab al-Sudan wa 'l-Bidan). The Muslim world did not need civil rights bills or affirmative action plans in order to provide Africans with equal advancement opportunity in the realm. Afro-Arabs gained prominence on all levels. Their renowned number included the above-mentioned Al-Jahiz (d. 869 C.E.), one of the greatest prose writers in classical Arabic literature and pioneer biologist; the poet Nusayb bin Riah; the financier Faraj Abu Kub; the black rulers of Muslim India, Malik Andil (d. 1494) and Malik Ambar (d. 1628); Yakub bin Yusuf al-Mansur (d. 1199), one of the greatest Moorish rulers of Spain; and Abu Hasan 'Ali (d. 1351), also known as Al-Sultan Al-Aswad, "The Black Sultan", who was patron of the arts and master of the Mediterranean after defeating the fleet of Admiral Godfrey Tenorio. (For these and many more, see J. A. Rogers, World's Great Men of Color, vol. I, Collier Books, N.Y., rev. ed. 1972.)

Racism is Ignorance

The sound tradition found at Bukhari 2:21 refutes decisively the contention that Islam sanctions any racial prejudice or discrimination. In this tradition, the prophet (peace be upon him) cogently identified racial abuse with ignorance. The Arabic word here, jahiliyyah, signifies foolisness, irrationality and any behavior in disregard to the facts. In Muslim terminology, jahiliyyah

*Incidentally, this refutes the claim that the obvious "Negroid" features of North Africans are merely the result of slavery. Rather, it is an ancient and indigenous phenomenon.

refers to the days of unbelief prior to the enlightenment of Islam; therefore, it is equivalent to kufr (unbelief). The verdict of the prophet shows that racism or racial discrimination is an act of unbelief as well as an indication of ignorance. Racial discrimination disregards the fact that all men are brothers racially. Since the prophet has pronounced racial discrimination to be ignorance, Islam cannot view any form of racism as scientific, intelligent or cultured. Rather, it is an act unworthy of a Muslim who has professed belief in the Creator of all mankind and in the Messenger whom He sent for the blessing of all mankind.

Categorically condemned as a jahiliy concept, racial discrimination has never been the policy of any Islamic state nor an approved practice of any Muslim. "People did not ask about race or origin but about deeds, character and righteousness. Among the Mamluks (slaves) who attained the highest state positions we find Armenian, Russian, Sicilian, Georgian, Circassian Tartar, Turk, Frank, Sudanese and Ethiopian... they represented all the colors of mankind... Racism, or a fanatic attachment to tribe, color, language, or culture, is rejected by the Message (of Muhammad) as a product of pre-Islamic idolatry. The prophet declares, 'He is not of us who preaches bigotry.' Islam rejects every form of bigotry. All loyalties are directed to the word of God, and no relation above the spiritual is recognized... no set of distinct racial traits with which we are familiar possessed at any time in human history a monopoly over intelligence, knowledge and originality."(17)

The Islamic Record in Africa

Muslim contributions to the development of Africa and African culture are many. Muslims refused to treat the African as an inferior, but, following the example of the prophet (peace be upon him), extended to him the hand of brotherhood and equality. The poor example of a small number of Muslim slave traders does not invalidate this. They obviously were following other than an Islamic example and were led by other than Islamic principles or motives. The overwhelming majority of Muslims refrained from such practices and in the true Islamic spirit continued to emancipate people from slavery and to liberate colonized people from colonization. Africans mastered Arabic and several native African languages adopted Arabic terms and expressions, such as Hausa, Yoruba and Swahili. "In providing a written language, a literate and learned administrative class, and above all, a bond of union that cut across ethnic considerations, Islam was a powerful factor in nation building in West Africa."(18) For example, "Northern Nigeria... (had) a well established system of government with laws and law courts and a fi-

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

S. Shahid Mufassir

nancial administration based on Islamic law."(19) African Muslims established international relations with the Islamic world, set up Islamic schools and colleges which gained wide fame. "Youth from all over the Muslim world came to Timbuktu (Mali, West Africa) to study law and surgery at the University of Sankore; scholars came from North Africa and Europe to confer with the learned historians and writers of the black empire. ('Abd al-Rahman) Al-Sa'di, a Timbuktu intellectual who wrote a history of the Sudan (Ta'rikh al-Sudan, 1655 CE)... had a private library of 1,600 volumes... The University of Sankore and other intellectual centers in Timbuktu had large and valuable collections of manuscripts in several languages. Scholars traveled to the Songhay city to check their Greek and Latin manuscripts."(20)

Ahmad Baba, born in Mali in 1556, composed many works on Islamic law and at least 13 of these are still in use by the 'ulama of West Africa. Another history of the western Sudan, Ta'rikh al-Fattash (History of the Seeker) had been composed in Arabic by the Malian Mahmud Kati, who was born in 1468. "This capacious activity of Muslim scholarship and writing has never ceased in West Africa, but has grown and spread with the passing of the years." (21) "The history of Islam in North Africa teems with examples of black rulers who achieved greatness in the opinion of contemporaries, irrespective of color or race. The history of Africa is full of examples of Sudanese jurists who attained the position of Imams, Qadis and Muftis, and whose books are known in the whole Muslim world. In Africa, Islam was an element of unification which stood in the face of attempts at disunity."(22)

Scholars agree that Islam played a fundamental role in nation building in Africa by providing the basis for unity and social justice. Even in the issue where Islam is much maligned by Western writers, that of slavery, Islam played a positive role. Because the goal of Islam is the emancipation of all men from the yokes of every type of servitude to men the Prophet and his companions liberated slaves and the Qur'an commends the emancipation of slaves in six separate verses. The abuses which are characteristic of slavery did not exist even when circumstances called for Muslims to take captives of war. Whether the slaves of Muslims were white or black, the condition of servitude carried no racial stigmas. Slavery was not rationalized on the basis of "innate inferiority" and the laws of Islamic states made emancipation easy. Among the Muslims, slavery never became a business enterprise or the staple of the economy and the trade in slaves has always been held to be contrary to Islamic teaching. By contrast, the official documents and pronouncements of the Church "supported the slave trade... Jesuits, Dominicans and Franciscans were heavily involved... The Moravian missionaries in the Islands held slaves without hesitation; the Baptists...

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

would not allow their earlier missionaries to deprecate ownership of slaves... Slave dealing was one of the most lucrative investments of English as of American Quakers."(23) It was not until the European slave trade that "slavery reached massive proportions, decimating whole tribes... Also, the Europeans were quick to formulate racial theories to jusitfy the traffic, classifying Africans as 'natural' slaves, foredoomed to such a lowly state by their inborn backwardness."(24)

The British abolished slavery in 1807, after it had become "less profitable and less vital to England... Prior to 1783, however, all classes in English society presented a united front with regard to the slave trade. The monarchy, the governed, the churches, public opinion in general, supported the slave trade."(25) Even afterward, this abolition was strongly objected to by men like Benjamin Disraeli, the Jewish prime minister (elected in 1868) who condemned the emancipation of slaves as "the greatest blunder ever committed by the English people." He wrote, "the movement of the middle class for the abolition of slavery was virtuous, but it was not wise. It was an ignorant movement." (Life of Lord George Bentinck)(26) But even before this British move, and long before the emancipation of slaves in America (1863), the Muslim government of Futa Toro in Senegal, West Africa, abolished slavery by law in 1788, despite the fierce opposition of French slave traders. The French "compalined to the Almamy (the Imam) asking him to change his mind and do away with the law. The Almamy refused to do so, and followed this refusal by sending back to the agents of the French slave-trading company a number of presents they had given him, adding that 'all the riches of that company would not make him change his mind.'"(27)

According to the Sierra Leone Studies, vol. 21, 1939, Muslim Africans had for long "participated in the suppression of the slave trade... the Sharif of Mecca had sent a letter to the king of the Fulas for circulation through all these Mandingo tribes, strictly prohibiting the selling of slaves — and which letter was also promulgated among the Yorubas, Fulanis and other neighboring tribes. The slave traffic was declared to be contrary to the teachings of Mohammed, which pronounce the most fearful denunciations of Allah's wrath in the world hereafter against those who persist in the traffic with the European nations." (pp. 18, 19)

God's Verdict on Race

While there is no "curse of Ham" in the Noble Qur'an, it does mention a black man rather prominently. This makes the Qur'an the only religious text in the world which has a whole chapter named after a member of the

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

S. Shahid Mufassir

African race: Luqman, upon whom God bestowed wisdom despite his humble status. "He is the type of perfect wisdom. It is said that he belonged to a humble station in life, being a slave or carpenter." (Qur'an translation by Yusuf Ali, p. 1082, note 3593.) According to Al-Mas'udi, he was a freed black slave. Other Arab traditions specify that he was a coal-black Ethiopian with wooly hair. (Cf. Qur'an translation by A. M. Daryabadi, vol. V, p. 656, note 264.) Eight verses of the holy book transmit the wisdom which God gave to Luqman (31:12-19). God's favor knows no racial boundaries.

The Qur'an, the word of man's Creator, has declared that racial differences exist for purely pleasant, positive reasons which are diametrically opposed to any form of discrimination or racism. There is not a single verse in the Qur'an which implies or says that racial differences are to be a natural means of segregation. God says:

We have honored (karramna) the children of Adam... and conferred on them special favors, above a great part of our creation.

(17:70)

No race or ethnic group comprising "the children of Adam" has been excluded from this honor or nobility (karamah) and superiority or preference (fadl) which God has conferred on mankind over the rest of creation.

As for varieties of color, Islam does not consider any hue of skin as being the result of a curse. All complexions are signs of God's creative power.

Among His signs (or, miracles: ayat) is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the differences in your languages and complexions. Truly these are signs for those who reflect.

(30:22)

No language or color is considered inferior and the very existence of diversity is indicative of God's miraculous, complex creative ability. The brown or black complexion is equally a miracle or marvel (ayah) as the white or yellow complexion.

Giving the greatest blow to all theories of racial discrimination, whether "scientific" or bigoted, God says further:

O mankind. We created you all from a single pair, and made you various races (shu'ub) and tribes so that you may be mutually acquainted.

(49:13)

"The accent is totally posivitive. The emphatic point, 'so that you (mankind) may be mutually acquainted,' is just one expression in Arabic: lita'arafu.

ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

RACE, RACISM AND ISLAM

In grammatical terms ta'arafa is a Form VI verb which emphasizes the mutual application of the verb sense. The verb root itself is 'arafa, which means 'to be acquainted with; to approve of; to appreciate; to be positive about.' The Qur'an, employing this expression lita'arafu, is making the revolutionary statement that God made the different races and peoples so that the variety in mankind would lead to mutual acquaintance, mutual approval, mutual appreciation, a positive attitude."(28)

Bernard Lewis passes over this phenomenal statement, having blurred its import by translating shu'ub (races) as the vague term "confederacies" and asserting that the main point being made by it is "clearly social rather than racial."(29) This assumption is incorrect. Shu'ub does refer to "races". Dr. A. J. Arberry so translates it in his The Koran Interpreted: "O mankind, We have created you male and female, and appointed you races and tribes . . ." The Muslim scholar Hafiz Ghulam Sarwar likewise renders this verse: "O ye mankind! Surely We have made you out of male and female. And We have made into races and tribes . . ."(30) In his commentary on this verse Maulana 'Abdul Majid Daryabadi (Vol. 6, The Taj Co., Karachi, Pakistan, 1957, p. 818) writes: "In plain speech, all races of men, Europeans, Asiatics and Africans; white, brown and black are equally His creation . . . This verse equally well demolishes the myth of a 'master race,' and completely supports the scientific finding that racial discrimination has no foundation in biological fact . . . this puts an end to the vast pseudo-science of 'racial biology' seeking to justify political ambitions (and) economic ends." And, according to Dr. Muhammad 'Abdul-Ra'uf, the essential point being made here is that "all people are equal in the eyes of God, and He wants them to treat each other as equal. Distinction between people on the basis of race, color or wealth or on any other basis is artificial and should not be tolerated."(31)

Islam insists that racial variety should be a means of mutual attraction, and this has been the function of racial variety during the many millenia in which the human population interbred extensively. Islam condemns racial discrimination as ignorance and goes beyond the requirement of mere racial tolerance. Islam calls for racial appreciation, mutual respect, a positive human brotherhood based on love for God and man.

arabic_text: وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً قَالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّمَاءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ قَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٣٠) وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ الْأَسْمَاءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنبِئُونِي بِأَسْمَاءِ هَٰؤُلَاءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٣١) قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ (٣٢) قَالَ يَا آدَمُ أَنبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ فَلَمَّا أَنبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ (٣٣) وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ (٣٤) وَقُلْنَا يَا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٣٥) فَأَزَلَّهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَاعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ (٣٦)

37 Then Adam received from his Lord certain commands whereby God redeemed him. Surely, He is the Redeemer, the Merciful. 38 I said, "Go down therefrom, all of you, and when My guidance comes to you, those who follow My guidance shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve. 39 As for those who disbelieve and reject My Revelations, they shall deserve the hellfire. They shall abide therein eternally."

(The Children of Israel)
40 O Children of Israel, be appreciative of the favors which I bestowed upon you; fulfill My covenant, that I may fulfill your covenant; you shall reverence Me; 41 You shall believe in what I reveal herein confirming what you have; do not be the first to reject it; you shall not trade away My revelations for a cheap material gain; you shall observe piety towards Me. 42 Do not confound the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth deliberately. 43 You shall observe the Salat prayers, pay the Zakat charity (due alms), and bow (in prayer) with those who bow. 44 Do you order people to be righteous, while forgetting your own selves, even though you know the scripture? Have you not any understanding? 45 Seek help in perseverence and in the Salat. Such is a difficult task, but not so for those who humble themselves; 46 who believe that they shall face their Lord; that they shall return to Him. 47 O Children of Israel, be appreciative of the favors which I bestowed upon you; I set you apart from all beings. 48 Beware of the day when no soul can avail another soul, no intercession can be accepted therefrom, no ransom can be paid, and no one can be helped.

(Deliverance from Egypt)
49 Recall that I saved you from the Pharaoh's people who inflicted severe persecution upon you; they slaughtered your sons and spared your daughters. Such was an exacting trial from your Lord. 50 Recall that I parted the sea for you; thus, I saved you and drowned the Pharaoh's people as you watched.

arabic_text: فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (٣٧) قُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٣٨) وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٣٩) يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ (٤٠) وَآمِنُوا بِمَا أَنزَلْتُ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ وَلَا تَكُونُوا أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍ بِهِ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا بِآيَاتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَإِيَّايَ فَاتَّقُونِ (٤١) وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا الْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٤٢) وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ (٤٣) أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (٤٤) وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ (٤٥) الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَاقُو رَبِّهِمْ وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ (٤٦) يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ (٤٧) وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (٤٨) وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُم مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَاءَكُمْ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُم بَلَاءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (٤٩) وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَأَنجَيْنَاكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ (٥٠)

51 Recall that when I summoned Moses for forty nights, you worshiped the calf in his absence, and you turned wicked. 52 Yet, I pardoned you thereafter, that you may be appreciative. 53 Recall that I gave Moses the scripture and the statute book, that you may be guided. 54 Recall that Moses told his followers, "You have wronged your souls by worshiping the calf. Therefore, you shall repent to your Creator; you shall kill your ego. This would be best for you with your Creator." Subsequently, God absolved you. Surely, He is the Absolver, most-Merciful. 55 When you said, "O Moses, we shall not believe unless we see God in person," the lightning struck you as you looked. 56 Then, I revived you after you died, that you may be appreciative.

(In Sinai)

57 I shaded you with clouds, and sent down to you manna and quails; "Eat from the good things I provide for you." Indeed, they did no harm to Me, but rather they harmed themselves. 58 When I said, "Go into this village and eat therefrom as you please; enter the gate in humbleness, and speak gently, that I may forgive your sins and reward the virtuous," 59 the evil ones distorted My commandments. Consequently, I showered the evil ones with wrath from the sky due to their wickedness. 60 Recall that when Moses sought water for his followers, I said, "Strike the rock with your staff." Whereupon, twelve springs gushed out therefrom. Thus, each of the tribes had their own water; "Eat and drink from God's provisions, and roam not the earth in corruption."

arabic_text: وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَنتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ (٥١) ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ (٥٢) وَإِذْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَالْفُرْقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ (٥٣) وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (٥٤) وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ (٥٥) ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاكُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ (٥٦) وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَىٰ كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ (٥٧) وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ادْخُلُوا هَٰذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ وَسَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٥٨) فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رِجْزًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ (٥٩) وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ فَانفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِن رِّزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ (٦٠)

61 When you told Moses, "We can no longer tolerate one kind of food; ask your Lord to produce for us earthly crops such as beans, cucumber, garlic, lentils, and onions," he said, "Do you wish to substitute that which is inferior for that which is good? Go down to the countryside wherein you may find your request." Thus, humiliation and poverty became their lot, and they incurred wrath from God. That, because they rejected God's commandments and because they slew the prophets unjustly; because they rebelled and transgressed. 62 Surely, those who believe; those who were Jewish, Christian, or Sabian; any among them who did believe in God and the hereafter, and did good works, shall receive their recompense from their Lord; they shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve.

(The Covenant)
63 Recall that I made a covenant with you, and raised Mount Sinai above you, saying, "You shall uphold this covenant strongly, and remember the contents thereof, that you may achieve piety." 64 But you turned away thereafter, and were it not for God's grace towards you and His mercy, you would have been destroyed. 65 You know what happened to those among you who desecrated the Sabbath; I said unto them, "You shall be despicable apes." 66 Thus, I set them up as an example for their generation, as well as subsequent generations, and an admonition for the pious.

(The Heifer)
67 When Moses said to his followers, "God commands you to sacrifice a heifer," they said, "Are you kidding us?" He said, "God forbid that I may be so ignorant." 68 They said, "Ask your Lord to show us what kind of heifer." Moses said, "He says that she is a heifer which is neither too old, nor too young; of an average age. You shall carry out this command."

arabic_text: وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ فَادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ مِن بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّائِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ اهْبِطُوا مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا وَّكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ (٦١) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالنَّصَارَىٰ وَالصَّابِئِينَ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٦٢) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (٦٣) ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَكُنتُم مِّنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (٦٤) وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ (٦٥) فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ (٦٦) وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ (٦٧) قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ (٦٨)

69 They said, "Ask your Lord to inform us of her color." Moses said, "He says that she shall be a yellow heifer; bright-colored and pleasant looking." 70 They said, "Ask your Lord to point her out for us. The heifers look alike; with God's help we shall find her." 71 Moses said, "He says that she is a heifer never humiliated in plowing the land or watering the crops; safe from any blemish." They said, "Now you have brought the truth;" they sacrificed her, though reluctantly. 72 Then, when you committed a murder and disputed among yourselves, God decided to uncover what you tried to conceal. 73 Thus, I said, "Strike the victim with part of that heifer." Whereupon, God revived the victim and showed you His signs, that you may understand. 74 Yet, your hearts hardened thereafter and became like rocks or even harder. For there are rocks from which rivers gush out; some rocks crack and gently release water; some rocks even stoop out of reverence for God. God is never unaware of anything you do.

(Distortion of the Scriptures)
75 How do you expect them to believe with you? Some of them used to hear the word of God then deliberately distort it with full understanding thereof. 76 When they meet the believers, they say, "We believe in this," but when in private with each other, they say, "Inform them not of the scripture revealed to you from God, lest they may use it to support their argument. Do you not understand?" 77 Do they not realize that God knows whatever they hide, as well as whatever they disclose? 78 Among them there are those who have no knowledge of the scripture; they may think that they know it, but in fact they do not. 79 Therefore, woe to those who fabricate the scripture with their own hands, then claim that such writings came from God, seeking thereby a cheap material gain. Woe to them as a consequence of their fabrications; woe to them as a consequence of their deeds.

arabic_text: قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ (٦٩) قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا وَإِنَّا إِن شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَمُهْتَدُونَ (٧٠) قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَا قَالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (٧١) وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْسًا فَادَّارَأْتُمْ فِيهَا وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ (٧٢) فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْيِي اللَّهُ الْمَوْتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (٧٣) ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (٧٤) أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا لَكُمْ وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُ مِن بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ (٧٥) وَإِذَا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ قَالُوا أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم بِمَا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لِيُحَاجُّوكُم بِهِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (٧٦) أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ (٧٧) وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا أَمَانِيَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ (٧٨) فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ الْكِتَابَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا فَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ (٧٩)

arabic_text: وَقَالُوا لَن تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَةً قُلْ أَتَّخَذْتُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ عَهْدًا فَلَن يُخْلِفَ اللَّهُ عَهْدَهُ أَمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٨٠) بَلَىٰ مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ فَأُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٨١) وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٨٢) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ لَا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّنكُمْ وَأَنتُم مُّعْرِضُونَ (٨٣) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ لَا تَسْفِكُونَ دِمَاءَكُمْ وَلَا تُخْرِجُونَ أَنفُسَكُم مِّن دِيَارِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ (٨٤) ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ هَٰؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَتُخْرِجُونَ فَرِيقًا مِّنكُم مِّن دِيَارِهِمْ تَظَاهَرُونَ عَلَيْهِم بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَإِن يَأْتُوكُمْ أُسَارَىٰ تُفَادُوهُمْ وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِخْرَاجُهُمْ أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَن يَفْعَلُ ذَٰلِكَ مِنكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ أَشَدِّ الْعَذَابِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (٨٥) أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا بِالْآخِرَةِ فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (٨٦) وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَقَفَّيْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ أَفَكُلَّمَا جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَىٰ أَنفُسُكُمُ اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ فَفَرِيقًا كَذَّبْتُمْ وَفَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ (٨٧)

arabic_text: وَقَالُوا قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ بَل لَّعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَقَلِيلًا مَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٨٨) وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِّنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ وَكَانُوا مِن قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُم مَّا عَرَفُوا كَفَرُوا بِهِ فَلَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ (٨٩) بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ أَن يَكْفُرُوا بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ بَغْيًا أَن يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ فَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ عَلَىٰ غَضَبٍ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ (٩٠) وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا نُؤْمِنُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَيَكْفُرُونَ بِمَا وَرَاءَهُ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ قُلْ فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنبِيَاءَ اللَّهِ مِن قَبْلُ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (٩١) وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَنتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ (٩٢) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَاسْمَعُوا قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُم بِهِ إِيمَانُكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (٩٣) قُلْ إِن كَانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ عِندَ اللَّهِ خَالِصَةً مِّن دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٩٤) وَلَن يَتَمَنَّوْهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ (٩٥) وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَاةٍ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ (٩٦) قُلْ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٩٧) مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّلَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِّلْكَافِرِينَ (٩٨)

COMMENTARY

Predestination:

In verse 30 of sura Al-Baqarah, the Almighty announces His intention to create man. A most significant statement in this verse, though invariably overlooked by most people, is the divine declaration, "I will place on earth . . ." Thus, the temporary abode of man on earth had been predestined, even before his creation. God knew in advance that Adam and Eve were going to break His law by eating from the forbidden tree (verse 36). He knew that they were going to sin; thereby disqualifying themselves from abiding in heaven, and deserving to be sent down to earth (verses 36 and 38). Man, on the other hand, did not possess such advance knowledge. As far as Adam and Eve were concerned, they were placed in heaven, and given a law to live by. Therefore, in a most profound way, these verses teach us that predestination is a quality of God; Man's life, every aspect of it is indeed predestined, BUT ONLY AS FAR AS GOD IS CONCERNED. As far as we are concerned, we have the absolute freedom of thought; the absolute freedom to believe in God or disbelieve (18:29; 25:57; 39:15; 41:40; 73:19; 74:37,55; 76:29; 78:39; 80:12; 81:28). It just happens that the Almighty has foreknowledge of what course each one of us is going to choose. The dimension of "time" represents one of the limitations within which the finite man lives. But it is a nonexistent dimension with regard to the infinite God. The Almighty, therefore, exists in the past, present, and future simultaneously. Because He is in the future now, He knows the exact destiny of each one of His Creatures.

Predestination is one of the most misunderstood concepts in Islam; both by Muslims and non-Muslims. It is also one of the most abused concepts by the enemies of God; the enemies of Islam. They abuse it to project Islam as a fatalistic faith, implying the absence of freedom of choice. Consequently, such fatalistic conception of Islam is a piece of ignorance common among too many teachers and students of theology in the West.

The law given to Adam and Eve is symbolized by the forbidden tree in verse 35. Since heaven is described in the Qur'an (2:25-26; 13:35; 47:15) in allegorical terms (see also the first issue of ISLAM, page 56), the tree mentioned in verse 35 must be an allegorical representation of God's law.

The facts about man's creation as stated in verses 30 through 39 provide another example of finalization of God's message in the Qur'an. Thus, the exact reasons behind the fall of Iblis (= Lucifer = Satan) are presented to mankind for the first time. No record of such facts exists in any of the previous scriptures. As mentioned in verse 34, Iblis refused to fall prostrate before

Adam along with the other angels, due to sheer arrogance. Even such prominent Christians as evangelist Billy Graham never knew the reasons behind the fall of Lucifer. In his 1974 Arizona Crusade (aired on television June 3, 1974 in the St. Louis, Missouri area), Mr. Graham declared, "We do not know why Lucifer rebelled. It seems that he led a group of angels in rebellion against God."

That Iblis is a fallen angel is abundantly clear from verse 34, "I said to the angels, 'Fall prostrate before Adam.'" Thus, the command to fall prostrate was directed to the angels. Had Iblis been other than an angel, therefore, he would not have been expected to obey such command. The fact that Iblis was held responsible for disobedience is clear evidence that he is a fallen angel. Some students of the Qur'an maintain that Iblis is a jinn; that angels do not disobey divine commands. If the source of this general belief is a Hadith or a tradition of which this commentator is unaware, this still does not necessitate that Iblis was not an angel. The Origin of
Islamic Jurisprudence

What some have erroneously termed "Islamic sects" are merely branches of one tree. There is but one school of jurisprudence in Islam, that based on the life and personal conduct of the prophet Muhammad (God's blessings and peace be upon him). It is from the extensive record of his exemplary life that the four well-known branches of Islamic jurisprudence evolved. The very initiation of these branches was approved by the Prophet himself. Thus, when he appointed Mu'adh b. Jabal as a viceroy in Yemen, the Prophet asked him, "How will you rule?" Mu'adh replied, "According to the Qur'an." The Prophet said, "What if you do not find a related rule in the Qur'an?" Mu'adh replied, "I will rule according to the sunnah (the Prophet's tradions)." The Prophet proceeded, "What if you do not find the ruling there?" Mu'adh said, "Then, I will have to depend on my personal thought and reasoning (ajtahidu)." The Prophet is reported to have been pleased and approved of Mu'adh's line of thinking.
In this article, the grand imam of Azhar reports on the origin and nature of the one tree of Islamic jurisprudence.

The final messenger of God (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him) practiced Islam as the Almighty wanted it to be practiced. He applied Islam to all aspects of his life; his actions, reactions, talk, feelings, and his daily conduct were all governed by Islam. The Prophet's companions followed his example very closely. This example of the Prophet was transmitted to us from his companions to their contemporaries and then onwards from generation to generation.

The companions of the Prophet explained the Islamic way of life as they saw the Prophet live it. They narrated everything he did or said with regard to all kinds of circumstances. As the Muslim nation expanded, the Muslims transmitted these traditions to the new areas. Eventually, many outstanding scholars evolved who specialized in researching, collecting, and recording the Prophet's traditions. Most of those scholars observed the highest

principles of scientific investigations to assure the accuracy and truthfulness of their sources. Their methods of collection and authentication of the Prophet's life have been highly esteemed by even the modern historians.

The Prophet's example was consistent with regard to certain specific situations. In other situations, however, he deliberately varied his mode of behavior. The situations where he was consistent include all the fard (the obligatory rites of worship). These encompass such rites as the method of fasting, the recitation of Qur'an during the salat, and the kneeling for "tashuhhud" recitation.

The variability in the Prophet's example was observed only with regard to the nonobligatory functions which are designated today as "sunnah." Thus, his conduct did not follow one specific methodology in such sunnahs as reciting supplications between the initial takbir of salat (saying, "Allah Akbar") and the opening sura (Al-Fatihah), and in his supplications as he fell prostrate in salat, and in the manner of placing the arms and hands during salat, and so forth. Such variations were observed also in many situations of daily life involving commerce, crimes, loans, usury, and personal relations. it is only around these variations in sunnah that the four branches of jurisprudence evolved. No differences whatsoever exist among the opinions of the imams Al-Shafi'i, Malik, Abu Hanifah, and ibn Hanbal concerning the obligatory duties. Their differences are found only in their personal interpretation and reasoning with regard to the nonobligatory actions and behavior of the Prophet.

These non-doctrinal differences of opinion among the four great imams have been grossly exaggerated by various groups who sought to create imaginary sects or divisions within Islam. Such exaggerations were intended mainly to divert the Muslims from their basic Islamic doctrines and, hence, from establishing the perfect society as inculcated by Islam. It was such groups who created, for example, the question of whether one should fold or unfold the arms while standing in salat. In the folding situation, the worshiper places the left hand on the stomach and the right hand on the back of the left hand. In the unfolding situation, the worshiper simply lets the arms hang down freely on the sides. This minor issue was magnified by some researchers beyond reasonable proportions, and led to lengthy and hot debates in certain Muslim countries. These arguments were finally terminated when one enlightened scholar raised the following questions to those involved in the controversy:
1. If the worshiper stood in salat with his arms extended straight forward, would that nullify the prayer?
2. If the arms were lifted completely upward, would that nullify the prayer?

THE ORIGIN OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE

3. If the arms were folded, would the prayer be nullified?
4. If the arms hang down on the sides, would that nullify the prayer?
When the debators unanimously agreed that the answer to each of these questions was "No", they realized the insignificance of their differences.

This question of placing one's arms during the salat prayer is a typical example of the subjects in which the great imams of jurisprudence expressed varied opinions. It is such differences of opinion, originating from the traditions of the Prophet, that became the basis of the branches in Islamic jurisprudence.

Clearly, all these branches, reflecting different personal interpretations, belong to one and the same tree. All the imams of jurisprudence had but a single model from which they derived their opinions. Only ignorance and narrow-mindedness would create separate schools of jurisprudence out of the one school, namely, the school of prophet Muhammad (God's peace and blessings be upon him). It is heartening to note that the era of false divisions within the school of Islamic jurisprudence has passed. It is a rarity nowadays to meet a Muslim who describes himself as a Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanafi, or Hanbali; the trend has been towards the one essential description: Muslim.

Who Qualifies as a Mujtahid?

By a mujtahid here is meant one who is scholarly qualified to set new rules and regulations to be followed by the Muslims everywhere. Some scholars have contended that the door of ijtihad (personal thought and reasoning which leads to new rules) has been closed; that the last mujtahids were the four well-known imams. Other scholars maintain that the door of ijtihad is always open. Some among the latter group, however, talk about ijtihad as if it were attainable by anyone. It is inconceivable that God's grace was limited to the four great imams with regard to ijtihad, since new circumstances are founded with each generation of humans. Therefore, any Muslim who satisfies certain exacting requirements can contribute to the rules and regulations known as Islamic jurisprudence, i.e., become a mujtahid. These requirements include:
1. Mastery of the Arabic language: The great imams of jurisprudence (e.g. Malik and Al-Shafi'i) were unrivaled masters of the Arabic linguistic sciences.
2. Memorization of the Qur'an, with full awareness of the complete message and regulations therein. This includes a high degree of knowledge of the various Qur'anic sciences such as the circumstances associated with the revelation of each verse or group of verses. Although the Qur'an was revealed for the guidance of all the people in all places and at all times, knowledge of the specific circumstances of revelation does help in reaching

'Abdul-Halim Mahmud

the correct interpretation.
3. Knowledge of the spoken sunnah, as well as the practical traditions of the Prophet (God's peace and blessings be upon him).
These requirements form the basic background needed by a Muslim before he or she can contribute correctly to Islamic jurisprudence.

The seriousness and the awesomeness of responsiblity in issuing new rules of jurisprudence can be appreciated if we reflect upon some of the Prophet's teachings in this regard. In Sahih Al-Shaykhan (well-known record of Hadith), the Prophet (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him) is reported as saying, "Whoever fabricates false rules from my teachings shall be committing a gross offense." Abu Hurayrah reported the Prophet's saying, "Whoever establishes a righteous tradition shall receive a reward equal to that due to all followers of such tradition, without reduction in their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil tradition shall incur sins equal to all the sins of those who follow such evil tradition, without reducing their guilt (reported in Sahih Muslim).

The overall purpose of ijtihad can be divided into 2 areas:
1. Establishing rules of Islamic jurisprudence relating to matters which took place during the Prophet's time. In this case, the purpose would be to find the Prophet's judgment regarding the matter in question. An example here would be the search for the exact manner of making ablution (wudu'), as performed by the Prophet (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him).
2. Establishing rules of Islamic jurisprudence dealing with current matters which did not exist during the Prophet's time. Even here, the rule-making process must depend on the Prophet's example through Qiyas (analogy).
The Qur'an and the sunnah of the holy Prophet provide an unlimited array of situations which can be used directly or indirectly in establishing current rules of Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, the Muslim never lacks the reference materials he needs to establish a given rule. Under all circumstances, the mujtahid must be a "follower," rather than an "initiator." For the Prophet's instructions to the mujtahids are, "you shall follow, not invent" when dealing with rules of Islamic jurisprudence.

Finally, it must be pointed out that ijtihad cannot succeed through knowledge alone. A mujtahid must be characterized first and foremost by a high standard of piety and righteousness. All the great imams who contributed positively to Islamic jurisprudence had in common a high level of genuine piety. Thus, the rules they have established for us represent no less than guidance from God to His sincere servants. Knowledge alone can never invoke such divine guidance, for God tells us, "only those who stand by God shall receive right guidance." (Qur'an 3:101).

It is said that one of his ancestors was a companion of the prophet Muhammad (God's blessings and peace be upon him) who moved to Herat with 'Asaf, son of Qays. Ansari's father, Abu Mansur Muhammad Ansari, became a permanent resident of Herat.

This states that Christ cannot come again and Christian hopes for the Kingdom of God cannot be fulfilled, until "Israel" is in complete control of Palestine, including Jerusalem, and the Temple of Solomon is rebuilt. IT is held that when a Seeker gives his heart and mind to the search, and disperses the mists that arise from tumultuous passions, Truth becomes brighter and brighter and fills the Soul with its light.

It is asserted that while reason is puzzling itself about mystery of consciousness, time, and space, the man of Faith is going forward from discovery to discovery, in the growing illumination of his heart.

But it must be recognised that this knowledge is only available to those whose eyes are fixed, like an archer, on the arrow and the object at which he aims, and that without purity of purpose and unceasing effort deliverance cannot be obtained.

In all ages and in all times men have sought and found truth. They have shown the way and means of attainment. But men have listened to the message with incredulity and continued the mad pursuit of sense objects.

Passions of body and mind govern men and kindle fires of desire, of greed, attachment, egoism and anger. These enslave and obscure the mind which must be freed, and restored to its pristine purity to reflect truth. The seekers of truth, therefore, concentrate all their strength in drawing away the mind from sense objects and to set it free from the dominations of fear and hate. Some follow the path of knowledge, and others the path of devotion, hoping to lose all sense of duality in the supreme uprising of love.

(from Preface of "The Invocations of 'Abdullah Ansari")
